---
title: Packaging
description: "Package an app as a plugin: flavours, Dockerfiles, hardware selectors, multi-architecture builds, and the arkitekt plugin build, stage and publish commands."
---


This page turns an app into a **plugin**: a container image that any Arkitekt server can install
and run through [Kabinet](/docs/build/concepts/services/kabinet), without you starting it by hand.

## Prerequisites

- An app that works with `arkitekt run prod` against your server
  ([Your first app](/docs/build/tutorials/python-first-app)).
- Docker, with the `buildx` plugin.
- An account on a container registry you can push to (Docker Hub by default).

## Flavours

A plugin is published as one or more **flavours**. A flavour is a build recipe: a `Dockerfile` plus
a `config.yaml` that says what hardware the image needs. One app can ship a `vanilla` CPU flavour
and a `gpu` flavour side by side, and the server installing it picks the flavour that fits its
hardware.

```bash
arkitekt plugin init --flavour vanilla
```

This creates:

```text
.arkitekt
└── flavours
    └── vanilla
        ├── Dockerfile
        └── config.yaml
```

| `plugin init` option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--flavour`, `-f` | Name of the flavour (`vanilla`, `gpu`, …) |
| `--template`, `-t` | Dockerfile template: `vanilla` (pip) or `uv` |
| `--arkitekt-version`, `-av` | The `arkitekt` version to pin in the Dockerfile |
| `--platform`, `-p` | Platforms to build for (repeatable). Default: `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` |
| `--no-multi-arch` | Build only for this machine's architecture |
| `--devcontainer`, `-dc` | Also generate a `.devcontainer/<flavour>/devcontainer.json` |

Add more flavours with `arkitekt plugin flavour add --flavour gpu --description "CUDA build"`.

### The Dockerfile

Arkitekt makes only two demands of the Dockerfile. It must contain your code with the app's
entrypoint (e.g. `app.py`) and the `.arkitekt` folder in the working directory, and it must have
`arkitekt` installed. The generated file is a good starting point. Edit it to add system libraries,
CUDA, model weights and so on. Paths in the Dockerfile are relative to the project root, not to the
flavour folder.

### `config.yaml` and selectors

```yaml
description: A CUDA build
dockerfile: Dockerfile
platforms:
  - linux/amd64
selectors:
  - kind: cuda
    compute_capability: "8.6"
    memory: 8000        # VRAM in MB
  - kind: ram
    min: 16000          # MB
```

**Selectors** constrain where a flavour may run. Every selector has a `kind`, `required` (default
`true`, a hard constraint) and `weight` (scores optional selectors). Add them with the CLI rather
than by hand:

```bash
arkitekt plugin selector add gpu --kind cuda --compute-capability 8.6 --vram 8000
```

| Kind | Fields |
|---|---|
| `cpu` | `min_count` (cores), `frequency` (MHz), `arch` (`amd64`, `arm64`, …) |
| `ram` | `min` (MB) |
| `cuda` | `compute_capability`, `cuda_version`, `memory` (VRAM MB), `count` (GPUs) |
| `rocm` | `api_version`, `api_thing` |
| `oneapi` | `oneapi_version` |
| `label` | `key`, `value`: matches a qualifier the server's operator put on a backend (e.g. `microscope: lightsheet`) |

A **service** your app needs (Mikro, Rekuest, …) is never a selector. It is a requirement of the
app, derived from `App(services=[...])`. `platforms` says what the image is *built* for, and a `cpu`
selector's `arch` says where it may *run*. Setting both so that they contradict is flagged by
`arkitekt plugin validate`.

## Build, stage, publish

```bash
arkitekt plugin validate   # check every flavour's Dockerfile and config.yaml
arkitekt plugin build      # build all flavours (or --flavour gpu)
arkitekt plugin stage      # run the local image against your server, as a deployment would
arkitekt plugin publish    # push the image(s) and record the release
```

- **`build`** builds each flavour's image. It then runs `arkitekt inspect` *inside* the image, so what
  gets published is exactly what that image would register (skip with `--no-inspect`). With several
  platforms, this machine's image is loaded locally and the others go to the build cache. A
  dependency without a wheel for the other architecture therefore fails here, not after publishing.
- **`stage`** runs the built image and connects it to your server, so you can test the container
  before anybody else sees it.
- **`publish`** pushes the images (as one multi-architecture manifest) and writes the release into
  the `.arkitekt` folder. Commit and push that folder. A Kabinet pointed at your repository discovers
  the release from it.

<Callout type="info" title="Multi-architecture builds">

Cross-building needs a `docker-container` buildx builder, which the CLI creates on first use as
`arkitekt`, and emulation for the foreign architecture:
`docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install all`. `publish` rebuilds from the current
sources using the cache, so publish from the same tree you built.

</Callout>

### Add an "Open in Arkitekt" badge

Put a badge at the top of the repository's README, so that anyone reading it can
hand the repository to their own Arkitekt in one click:

```markdown
[![Open in Arkitekt](https://arkitekt.live/img/badge/open-in-arkitekt.svg)](https://arkitekt.live/deeplink?orkestrator=%2Fkabinet%2Frepos%2Finstall%3Frepo%3DYOUR-USER%252FYOUR-REPO)
```

Replace `YOUR-USER` and `YOUR-REPO`; the `%252F` between them is an encoded
slash and has to stay encoded. The badge image is the same for every
repository — what it opens is carried by the link, not by the picture.

Clicking it opens the reader's own Orkestrator on the install prompt for your
repository, where they can add it to their Kabinet. Readers without Orkestrator
land on arkitekt.live instead, which tells them how to get it.

<Callout type="info" title="Let Orkestrator write it for you">

Orkestrator can produce the snippet: open the repository under **Kabinet →
Repos** and use **Copy README badge**.

</Callout>

<Callout type="warn" title="On Versioning">

One version of an app has exactly one release. To publish changes, bump the version in `App(...)`
in your entrypoint, then build and publish again. [Why we version](/docs/deploy/concepts/versioning)
explains why a version, once published, must not change.

</Callout>

<Callout type="info" title="On Registries">

Images are pushed to Docker Hub by default. The release metadata lives in your repository's
`.arkitekt` folder, so any server that can read the repository and pull the image can install the
plugin. There is no central plugin index yet.

</Callout>

## Next

The app is now installable. Readers of your repository can add it to their Kabinet in one click with
the badge above. See [Kabinet](/docs/build/concepts/services/kabinet) for how servers pull and run plugin
images.
